summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The Nicene Creed (the formalized textual kernel) read by centralized imperial/church authorities as a strict mandate for structural uniformity and heresy suppression (an extractive authority mechanism) versus read by localized or reformist communities as a purely spiritual, non-coercive confession of faith. This represents an authority-grounding contest over the exact limits of a shared, unchangeable commitment[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (the codified international legal kernel) read by recognized Nuclear Weapon States as primarily a mandate to prevent horizontal proliferation (enforcing a geopolitical oligopoly) versus read by Non-Nuclear Weapon States as a reciprocal pact requiring immediate, good-faith disarmament. The competing readings of the exact same treaty emit entirely different structural constraints and victim sets[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The US Internal Revenue Code Section 469 (the fixed statutory kernel) read by the IRS as a narrow, strictly gated exception requiring rigorous, verifiable material participation (a high-friction boundary) versus read by the real estate industry and tax strategists as a broad, structurally exploitable loophole for passive loss deduction (a wealth-extraction scaffold). Competing readings of the same legal text determine the extraction of billions in tax liabilities[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The multilateral trade agreement text (the shared legal kernel) read by multinational corporations as an overriding mandate for unfettered capital mobility and regulatory harmonization (an extraction mechanism) versus read by domestic labor/environmental agencies as an agreement still subordinate to sovereign local protections. The contest defines the jurisdictional boundaries of the state[cite: 2, 3].
